description:
Execute JavaScript against Xquik's X (Twitter) API. Reads cost 1 credit per result, 2 per analyzed post & 5 per article. 1,000 credits cost $0.12-$0.15. Writes cost 10 credits & posts from 30. Empty & failed reads are free. First use the search tool to find endpoints, parameters & response schemas. The sandbox declares `interface XquikRequest { path: string; method?: "GET" | "POST" | "PUT" | "PATCH" | "DELETE"; query?: Record<string, string | number | boolean | undefined>; body?: unknown } declare const xquik: { result: unknown; request<T = unknown>(options: XquikRequest): Promise<T> }`. request() returns the body as the API sends it, as the response schema from search describes it. code is an async arrow function. Fields use snake_case, & camelCase reads work too. A missing field reads as undefined & warns with the available keys. An absent field may need a request parameter. Output holds up to 24,000 characters, so large arrays fit after projection. A call ends at 55 s, waits included. A post can take 1 minute. Wait between calls. Paged reads return a cursor. Run independent reads with Promise.all. A result_id from an earlier answer lets a later call project its saved data through xquik.result. Authentication & idempotency headers are injected, so code holds no credentials. The sandbox has no filesystem or general network access. A failed request throws an Error naming its method, path, HTTP status & request ID, then the API's error body.

Example
```js
async () => xquik.request({ path: "<path from search>" })
```

code.description: JavaScript async arrow function that calls xquik.request().

result_id.description: Saved result ID from an earlier answer. Leave it out unless an answer gave you one. Read its data through xquik.result.

warnings.description: Missing field names mapped to available keys. Optional fields may require explicit request parameters. Absence does not prove the data is unavailable.
